course.title: Housekeeping and Commercial Cleaning English
course.summary: Confirm assigned cleaning work, respect occupied spaces, clarify product information, report building concerns, manage supplies, and give accurate completion updates.
course.roles: Housekeeping attendants, commercial cleaners, custodial staff, and cleaning team members
course.scope_note: All room numbers, buildings, times, counts, policies, and incidents are fictional English practice, not cleaning certification, chemical-use instruction, medical advice, or access authorization. Follow employer training and site procedures for products, equipment, privacy, waste, and hazards. Do not infer permission to enter, mix products, handle unknown waste, or repair equipment. This course addresses frontline cleaning exchanges rather than hospitality management.

sources.title: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Occupational Outlook Handbook: Janitors and Building Cleaners
O*NET OnLine: Maids and Housekeeping Cleaners

modules.title: Confirming the assignment and its limits
collocations: confirm the assigned area: identify exactly which space belongs to the task
clarify the service scope: check which work is included
prioritize the requested room: agree which assigned space comes first
distinguish a spot from the whole surface: define the extent of a cleaning request

case.brief: A commercial assignment says 'conference room: tables and floor.' The client asks for 'everything' before a 3:00 meeting. The worker is assigned table surfaces and the floor, not high windows or personal equipment. The supervisor can clarify extra work; the meeting time doesn't expand permission.
case.model: The assignment covers the conference-room table surfaces and floor. When you say everything, are you also asking about the high windows and personal equipment? Those aren't included in my current task list. I can complete the listed work and ask my supervisor to review the additional request before anyone promises it for three o'clock.

workshop.title: Turn 'everything' into named tasks
workshop.goal: Clarify the requested surfaces and the boundary of the current assignment.
workshop.explanation: A broad request may contain extra work or items the cleaner should not move. Name the included work and ask about the rest.
frames: When you say ___, which surfaces do you mean?
I'll ask the supervisor whether ___ can be added.
workshop.after: I'll clean the listed tables and floor; the additional items need a scope check.
workshop.reason: The revised statement gives a precise commitment.

questions.prompt:
Client: By everything, I also meant the high windows.
Cleaner: Those tasks are ____ my current assignment.
feedback: 'Within' would put those extra tasks inside the listed scope.
Correct. The current assignment covers tables and floor, not high windows.
'Included in' would incorrectly claim the extra work was assigned.
'Covered by' would also include work outside the stated scope.

questions.prompt:
Supervisor: Is the client asking for the whole carpet to be cleaned?
Cleaner: No, just one marked patch. The request is for ____.
feedback: This covers the whole room rather than the one patch.
Inspection assesses the carpet; the request specifically asks for cleaning.
Full carpet cleaning extends beyond the patch the client identified.
Correct. Spot cleaning targets the particular marked area.

workshop.role_b: Client: you want table surfaces and floor ready first; windows are an extra request.
workshop.challenge: The client adds laptops to 'tables.' Clarify that cleaning around personal equipment differs from handling it.

modules.title: Respecting access and occupied spaces
collocations: request permission to enter: ask before entering where permission is required
agree a return time: arrange when to offer service again
respect a declined service: accept the occupant's stated choice
confirm the access window: verify when the room is available for work

case.brief: A guest in room 312 declines cleaning at 10:00 because of a call until 11:00. The attendant's return window is 11:15-11:30. The guest can choose a visit in that window or fresh towels at the door now. No room entry is authorized by this conversation alone.
case.model: I understand you're on a call until eleven. I can offer a return between eleven fifteen and eleven thirty, or bring fresh towels to the door now if that is all you need. Which would you prefer? I'll record your choice, and we'll still follow the room-access arrangements when I return.

workshop.title: Offer a return window without overriding privacy
workshop.goal: Agree a practical service choice with an occupant.
workshop.explanation: A return appointment and permission to enter are separate. State the available window instead of promising an exact minute you can't control.
frames: Would you prefer no room service today?
workshop.after: I can return between eleven fifteen and eleven thirty; would that suit you?
workshop.reason: The guest gets a choice rather than an announced entry.

questions.prompt:
Guest: Your return is between eleven fifteen and eleven thirty?
Attendant: Yes, that's a ____.
feedback: A fifteen-minute interval is not one guaranteed minute.
The guest is checking an offered visit, not refusing it.
Correct. A window gives a range of times.
The visit has not yet taken place.

questions.prompt:
Attendant: Would you prefer fresh towels ____ room cleaning today?
Guest: Yes, towels only.
feedback: Correct. The guest chooses towels as the replacement service.
This would request both services, unlike 'towels only'.
This adds cleaning rather than replacing it.
This keeps both services rather than towels alone.

workshop.role_b: Guest: choose towels only today and decline a later room-cleaning visit.
workshop.challenge: The guest says 'after my call' without confirming a time. Offer the actual window again.

modules.title: Clarifying product and task information
collocations: identify the product: confirm the exact container and product name
consult the current label: use information for the product actually present
ask for the task standard: clarify what the assignment requires
report missing information: explain which required detail cannot be confirmed

case.brief: A bottle on the cart has an unreadable label. A colleague identifies it by color, but two products use similar bottles. The cleaner has not used it. The supervisor can identify it and provide the relevant product information or a clearly identified replacement. No chemical steps are taught.
case.model: I can't identify this bottle from its unreadable label, and its color doesn't resolve which product it contains. I haven't used it. Could you help confirm the product and its current information, or provide a clearly identified replacement? I need that resolved before I continue the assigned task with this bottle.

workshop.title: Ask for identification, not a guess
workshop.goal: Describe missing product information and request qualified help.
workshop.explanation: The same color or bottle shape can belong to different products. Knowing a nickname isn't the same as identifying the actual container.
frames: The label doesn't let me confirm ___.
Could you provide the current ___ for this product?
workshop.before: It's the blue one, so I know it.
workshop.after: The label is unreadable; color alone doesn't identify this product.
workshop.reason: The revised explanation names the unresolved fact.

questions.prompt:
Colleague: Both bottles are blue. Is that enough to identify this one?
Cleaner: Its identity is still ____.
feedback: The case gives two products with similar color.
Correct. Appearance hasn't established the actual product identity.
The label is explicitly described as unreadable.
No readable label match has been obtained.

questions.prompt:
Cleaner: This Safety Data Sheet names Product A, but the bottle label names Product B.
Supervisor: Please obtain ____ for the product-information check.
feedback: The room assignment identifies work, not the product's hazard information.
A newer document for Product A still doesn't match Product B.
Correct. The Safety Data Sheet must identify the actual product being checked.
A matching delivery note doesn't replace the product's Safety Data Sheet.

workshop.role_b: Colleague: you recognize the bottle color but cannot confirm its contents.
workshop.challenge: The colleague offers a nickname. Request the exact product information from the supervisor.

modules.title: Reporting faults and unsafe access
collocations: describe the observed condition: say what you saw without inventing a cause
give an exact location: identify floor, room, or nearby landmark
report a recurrence: say that the same observed condition appeared again
keep an area status clear: distinguish cleaned, restricted, and awaiting review

case.brief: Water is visible on the floor outside washroom B, beside the east stair door. The cleaner doesn't know the source and has reported it under site arrangements. The supervisor needs an exact location and confirmation that the area has not been declared ready. No plumbing diagnosis or cleanup method is requested.
case.model: There is water on the floor outside washroom B, beside the east stair door. I don't know its source, and I haven't marked that area ready. Please arrange the appropriate site response and tell me who is taking the follow-up. I'll report the location and current restriction clearly to the next team.

workshop.title: Give the response team useful facts
workshop.goal: Report location, observation, and unresolved status without a technical diagnosis.
workshop.explanation: 'Water near a door' is less useful than a specific washroom and landmark. Request the appropriate responder rather than offering repair steps.
frames: Who is handling ___, and what should I report about access?
workshop.after: Water is visible outside washroom B beside the east stair door; the source is unknown.
workshop.reason: The report gives a checkable location without claiming a cause.

questions.prompt:
Supervisor: Do you know where the water came from?
Cleaner: No. Its source is ____.
feedback: No pipe fault has been established from the observation.
No spill has been confirmed as the water's source.
Correct. The cleaner observed water without establishing its cause.
Earlier cleaning doesn't establish the cause of the present water.

questions.prompt:
Supervisor: Is the water inside washroom B?
Cleaner: No, it's ____ washroom B, beside the east stair door.
feedback: Inside contradicts the cleaner's correction and the stated location.
No water above the washroom has been reported.
Correct. Outside locates the water beyond the washroom entrance.
Opposite means across from it, which the case doesn't establish.

workshop.role_b: Supervisor: ask for the precise location and accept the response-team contact.
workshop.challenge: A passerby says the floor was cleaned earlier. Explain why the present water still needs reporting.

modules.title: Handling found items and privacy questions
collocations: report a found item: notify the responsible person of an unattended object
describe visible features: state what can be observed without searching private contents
record the found location: preserve where the object was discovered
confirm receipt of the item: verify who accepted the transfer

case.brief: An attendant finds a closed black glasses case beneath the chair in room 214 after checkout. The owner is unknown. The attendant should report visible details without opening it and transfer it to the designated lost-property receiver, who can confirm receipt. Don't identify an owner from a guess.
case.model: I found a closed black glasses case beneath the chair in room two-fourteen. I haven't opened it, and I don't know whose it is. Could you receive it through the lost-property arrangement and confirm the transfer? Please keep the found location separate from its storage location so any later inquiry uses the correct details.

workshop.title: Transfer an item without inventing its owner
workshop.goal: Give observable details and obtain a receiving acknowledgment.
workshop.explanation: Finding an item in a room doesn't prove who owns it. Describe the exterior and location without inspecting private contents or publicly disclosing guest information.
workshop.after: It's a closed black glasses case; the owner is unconfirmed.
workshop.reason: The description separates observation from an ownership guess.

questions.prompt:
Receiver: Where was the case found?
Attendant: ____ the chair in room 214.
feedback: The case wasn't found inside the chair.
Correct. 'Under' matches the stated location beneath the chair.
The case wasn't found on top of it.
Beside means next to, not beneath, the chair.

questions.prompt:
Attendant: Have you accepted the item?
Receiver: Yes, ____.
options: I can describe where it was found
I've received the closed black case
feedback: Being told about an item doesn't confirm its receipt.
A future intention doesn't confirm acceptance has happened now.
Knowing the found location doesn't acknowledge accepting custody.
Correct. This names the item and confirms completed receipt.

workshop.role_b: Receiver: accept the closed case and repeat the found location; ownership remains unknown.
workshop.challenge: A colleague asks you to name the previous guest in a public area. Keep the inquiry with the designated receiver.

modules.title: Counting linen and replenishing supplies
collocations: count by item type: keep different supplies in separate totals
replenish the dispenser: restore the assigned supply without assuming a different product fits
report the shortfall: state how many items are missing from the target
confirm an allocation: identify supplies assigned to a particular floor or task

case.brief: The third-floor cart target is twelve bath towels and eight hand towels. The attendant counts nine bath towels and eight hand towels. A laundry delivery is expected but not confirmed. Report the three-bath-towel shortfall without calling all linen unavailable.
case.model: The cart has nine bath towels and eight hand towels. Against today's target of twelve and eight, we're short three bath towels; the hand-towel count is complete. A laundry delivery is expected, but its arrival isn't confirmed. Could you check whether three bath towels can be allocated from available stock?

workshop.title: Give useful counts, not a general shortage
workshop.goal: State target, actual count, and difference for each item.
workshop.explanation: Separate item types and distinguish an expected delivery from available stock. A shortfall in one item doesn't mean every linen item is unavailable.
frames: We have ___ against a target of ___.
workshop.after: We're three bath towels short; all eight hand towels are present.
workshop.reason: The next person knows exactly what needs replenishment.

questions.prompt:
Lead: Twelve bath towels are needed and nine are on the cart.
Attendant: The shortfall is ____.
feedback: Correct. Twelve minus nine leaves three bath towels.
Nine is the amount present, not the missing amount.
The hand-towel count is already complete.
This uses the wrong item and quantity.

questions.prompt:
Lead: Has laundry confirmed when the delivery will arrive?
Attendant: No. It is ____.
feedback: This conflicts with the explicit absence of confirmation.
An unconfirmed time doesn't mean the delivery was canceled.
No completed arrival has been reported in the scenario.
Correct. This preserves the expected timing without claiming verification.

workshop.role_b: Lead: you can check storage, but cannot promise the laundry arrival time.
workshop.challenge: Another floor requests two towels from this cart. Explain the effect on its count before any reassignment.

modules.title: Responding to a quality concern
collocations: acknowledge the specific concern: name the mark or missed area the person reports
ask for the exact location: identify which surface needs attention
check against the task requirement: compare the result with the assigned standard
confirm the correction: ask whether the reported issue has been addressed

case.brief: A client reports streaks on the interior glass panel beside office 8, cleaned earlier that day. The cleaner can acknowledge the reported result and ask the lead to arrange a check and appropriate rework. The cause is unknown; the client is available to point out the panel.
case.model: Thank you for showing me the streaks on the interior panel beside office eight. That is the panel on today's completed task list. I'm sorry the result needs attention. I'll ask our lead to check it and arrange the appropriate rework. I don't know the cause yet, so I'll report the visible marks rather than guess.

workshop.title: Address the result without arguing about effort
workshop.goal: Clarify a quality concern and agree a check of the specific area.
workshop.explanation: 'It was cleaned' doesn't mean every result meets the task requirement. Listen for the exact surface and defect instead of defending how long the task took.
frames: Could you show me the exact ___?
I can see the ___ you mean.
I'll ask for a check of ___, not assume ___.
workshop.after: That panel was cleaned earlier; I can see the streaks you're pointing out.
workshop.reason: The revision acknowledges both earlier work and the present concern.

questions.prompt:
Client: I mean visible wipe-like lines across the glass, not a coating, grooves, or missing pieces.
Cleaner: So you're describing ____.
feedback: Residue names material left behind, not the specific line pattern described.
Scratches are surface damage such as grooves, which the client excludes.
Correct. Streaks are the visible lines or uneven wipe marks described.
Chips involve missing pieces of material, which the client excludes.

questions.prompt:
Cleaner: I'll report what I can see, ____ guess the cause.
Client: Thank you.
feedback: 'Because of' needs a noun phrase, not this verb form.
Correct. This contrasts observation with an unsupported explanation.
This would add guessing to the reported observation.
This also adds guessing and requires a different verb form.

workshop.role_b: Client: point to the inside panel beside office 8 and ask when someone can check it.
workshop.challenge: The client says all windows must be poor. Keep the confirmed concern limited to the identified panel.

modules.title: Giving a clear end-of-shift handover
collocations: hand over the remaining area: identify unfinished work and its next owner
distinguish cleaned from inspected: keep task completion separate from a later check
record an access limitation: state what prevented work in a particular area
confirm who takes over: obtain acknowledgment from the receiving worker

case.brief: Rooms 301 and 302 have been cleaned; 302 awaits the supervisor's inspection. Room 303 was inaccessible and not cleaned. The incoming attendant can accept 303's access follow-up, while the supervisor owns 302's inspection. Report each status separately without deciding room release.
case.model: Room three-oh-one is cleaned. Three-oh-two is also cleaned, but the supervisor's inspection is still pending. Three-oh-three was inaccessible and hasn't been cleaned. Can you take the access follow-up for three-oh-three? I'll confirm the inspection request with the supervisor; please don't describe that pending check as a completed sign-off or a room-release decision.

workshop.title: Report the stage, not a vague 'ready'
workshop.goal: Give each area a precise status and a named follow-up.
workshop.explanation: Cleaned, inspected, and released can be separate statuses under a site's arrangements. Do not turn a completed cleaning task into a broader authorization.
frames: Can you accept the follow-up for ___?
workshop.after: 301 is cleaned; 302 awaits inspection; 303 remains uncleaned due to access.
workshop.reason: The statuses let the next worker act without guessing.

questions.prompt:
Incoming attendant: Is 302's inspection complete?
Outgoing attendant: It's cleaned, but inspection is ____.
feedback: No inspection sign-off has been confirmed in the case.
The required check remains open despite completed cleaning.
Scheduling a check doesn't establish that it was completed.
Correct. The inspection remains unfinished despite completed cleaning.

questions.prompt:
Outgoing attendant: Can you take 303's access follow-up?
Incoming attendant: Yes, ____.
options: I'll confirm access and update its status
I sent someone a note about access
I remember seeing the access request
I thought it belonged to the earlier shift
feedback: Correct. This explicitly accepts the named follow-up and reporting task.
Sending a note doesn't identify who now accepts the task.
Remembering a request doesn't commit to carrying it out.
This states a previous assumption rather than accepting responsibility.

workshop.role_b: Incoming attendant: accept 303's access question and repeat that its cleaning hasn't started.
workshop.challenge: A caller asks whether 302 can be released. Direct the release question to the responsible person.

jargon.definition: A list identifying the rooms, areas, or cleaning tasks allocated to a worker.
jargon.group: Confirming the assignment and its limits

jargon.definition: The specific cleaning work included in an assignment or agreement.
jargon.group: Confirming the assignment and its limits

jargon.definition: A surface or item frequently touched by people, such as a handle.
jargon.group: Confirming the assignment and its limits

jargon.definition: Cleaning a particular marked or affected area rather than the entire surface.
jargon.group: Confirming the assignment and its limits

jargon.definition: A sign communicating an occupant's request not to be disturbed; entry rules remain site-specific.
A room currently in use by a guest or other occupant.
An agreed period during which a space can be entered for assigned work.
An occupant's decision to decline an offered cleaning visit or task.
The information attached to a cleaning product identifying it and its stated use and warnings.
A document describing a chemical product's hazards and related safety information; often shortened to SDS.
Removing dirt and other unwanted material from a surface.
A process intended to inactivate specified microorganisms under the product's stated conditions; not synonymous with ordinary cleaning.
A report describing a condition that may cause harm and needs the appropriate response.
A request for the responsible team to assess or repair a building or equipment problem.
A sign identifying equipment or an area as unavailable for use.
The specific location impacted by a reported problem.
Items found without their owner present and handled through the site's return arrangements.
jargon.group: Handling found items and privacy questions

jargon.definition: A factual account of a found object's visible identifying features.
jargon.group: Handling found items and privacy questions

jargon.definition: The precise place where an item was discovered, separate from where it is later stored.
jargon.group: Handling found items and privacy questions

jargon.definition: A record identifying who received or held an item during its transfer.
jargon.group: Handling found items and privacy questions

jargon.definition: Fabric items used in rooms or service areas, such as sheets and towels.
Adding supplies to replace what has been used or is missing.
The target quantity of a supply used as a stocking reference.
A difference between a recorded quantity and the quantity actually counted.
A check of completed work against the relevant task requirements.
Work repeated or corrected because the first result didn't meet the specified requirement.
Material left on a surface after use or a cleaning task.
A visible line or uneven mark on a surface such as glass.
The recorded stage of a room's service, such as not started, in progress, or awaiting inspection.
Work that has not yet been completed.
A record showing which assigned work was actually completed and any relevant limitations.
A recorded confirmation by the designated person that a specified check or task meets its requirement.

conversations.title: Everything has a boundary
conversations.setting: The conference-room assignment in the case.
turns: Client
Could you clean everything in this conference room before our three o'clock meeting?
Cleaner
My assignment sheet lists tables and floor. Which other items did you mean?
Client
The high windows look marked, and there are laptops on some of the tables.
Cleaner
Those aren't included in my task list. I can ask my supervisor about the additional request.
Client
Please put the tables and floor first. The meeting can't move to another room.
Cleaner
I can prioritize that assigned work, but I won't handle laptops without the site's instructions.
Client
We'll ask their owners to clear them. Can you report any table area you couldn't reach?
Cleaner
Yes. I'll describe any inaccessible surfaces rather than mark the whole room complete.
Client
And please ask about the windows without promising they'll be finished before the meeting.
Cleaner
I will. The listed table and floor work remains my assignment; the windows need review.

conversations.title: A spot or the whole carpet?
conversations.setting: A cleaner clarifies a client's request about a marked carpet.
turns: Cleaner
You asked me to address the carpet. Do you mean this patch or the entire room?
Client
This small patch beside the door is the issue. The rest is on the usual schedule.
Cleaner
Thank you. I'll report a spot-cleaning request for that patch, not a whole-room treatment.
Client
Can you guarantee the mark will disappear before the visitors arrive this afternoon?
Cleaner
I can't promise that outcome. I'll ask the supervisor about the suitable work and timing.
Client
Please tell them it's near the entrance, where visitors will see it first.
Cleaner
I'll give the exact location and note that you haven't requested the whole carpet today.
Client
That's right. I want the particular mark assessed without changing the full cleaning schedule.
Cleaner
Is the visitor arrival time two o'clock, as shown on the room booking?
Client
Yes, two o'clock. Please use that time when you discuss the request with your supervisor.

conversations.title: Touchpoints in the corridor
conversations.setting: A team member clarifies the location of a daily task.
turns: Cleaner
The sheet says corridor touchpoints. Does that include the handles inside the private offices?
Team lead
Today's assignment covers shared corridor handles and railings, not entry into the private offices.
Cleaner
Thanks. I wanted to check the boundary before assuming the office doors were included.
Team lead
The shared-side handles are included, but office access is a separate arrangement for another shift.
Cleaner
I'll describe the task as the shared corridor touchpoints, with no private-office entry.
Team lead
Exactly. Please also identify which corridor section you're covering so we don't duplicate the work.
Cleaner
I'll take the east corridor between the lifts and the meeting-room entrance this shift.
Team lead
Then I'll assign the west corridor to Noor and leave the private-office list separate.
Cleaner
If a tenant asks me to add an office, I'll refer that extra request to you.
Team lead
Please do. We can clarify access and scope before changing either worker's assignment.

additional_scenario.title: Furniture is not part of the floor request
additional_scenario.brief: A client asks for a meeting-room floor cleaned but heavy display units block one corner. The cleaner isn't assigned to move them. The supervisor can review access.
additional_scenario.role_b: Client: arrange staff assistance or accept a recorded limitation.
additional_scenario.opening_line: I can reach the open floor, but that corner is blocked by the display units.
additional_scenario.complication: The client assumes 'floor cleaning' includes moving all furniture.
success_checks: Avoid assuming permission or ability to move heavy units.
Agree who resolves access and how completion is described.

conversations.title: A service choice at the door
conversations.setting: Room 312 at 10:00, following the case.
turns: Attendant
Good morning. Is now a convenient time to clean your room, or should I return?
Guest
I'm on a work call until eleven, so I can't have the room cleaned now.
Attendant
I can return between eleven fifteen and eleven thirty, or bring towels to the door now.
Guest
Towels only would be better today. I don't need a later cleaning visit.
Attendant
Certainly. How many fresh towels would you like delivered without entering the room?
Guest
Two bath towels, please. I can take them at the door once you return.
Attendant
I'll bring two and record that you declined room cleaning today, not all service.
Guest
Thank you. Please don't interpret my declining cleaning as permission to enter after the call.
Attendant
Understood. I'll leave the room entry unchanged and knock when I bring the towels.
Guest
That works. I can briefly answer the door for them without interrupting the whole call.

conversations.title: A meeting runs beyond the access window
conversations.setting: A cleaner negotiates access with an office occupant.
turns: Cleaner
Our access window starts at six, but I can see your meeting is still running.
Office occupant
It may take another twenty minutes. Could you start cleaning around us while we finish?
Cleaner
I need to check whether occupied cleaning is suitable under this site's arrangement.
Office occupant
Then could you work on the corridor first and return after we leave?
Cleaner
The corridor is on my assignment, so I can change that order of work.
Office occupant
Thank you. We expect to leave by six twenty, but I can't guarantee that yet.
Cleaner
I'll return to ask at six twenty rather than assume the room has become available.
Office occupant
Please do. I'll tell the team someone will check, not announce cleaning as already started.
Cleaner
If you're still here, I'll report the access delay and discuss the remaining window with my lead.
Office occupant
That sounds reasonable. You can complete the corridor while we finish the meeting.

conversations.title: A sign and a verbal message conflict
conversations.setting: An attendant asks the supervisor about contradictory room-access information.
turns: Attendant
Room 418 still has a do-not-disturb notice, but my sheet says service requested this morning.
Supervisor
Do you have a current message from the guest resolving that difference, or only the sheet?
Attendant
Only the sheet. I haven't entered or assumed the sign was left there accidentally.
Supervisor
Thank you. We'll clarify the guest's current preference through the property's access arrangements.
Attendant
Should I mark the room as cleaned because it appeared on the requested-service list?
Supervisor
No. Mark the service as not completed due to unresolved access, using our status categories.
Attendant
I'll state that the notice is present and the request on the sheet needs clarification.
Supervisor
Exactly. Don't turn either piece of information into a guess about the guest's intentions.
Attendant
I'll move to my next available room while you check the access question.
Supervisor
Please do. I'll give you a clear update rather than leave you waiting at that door.

additional_scenario.title: A locked meeting room
additional_scenario.brief: A cleaner has an assignment for room B at 7:00, but the door is locked and the cleaner has no approved access method. The office contact can arrange access at 7:30.
additional_scenario.role_a: Cleaner: explain the obstacle and available work elsewhere.
additional_scenario.role_b: Office contact: offer 7:30 access; do not ask the cleaner to improvise entry.
additional_scenario.opening_line: The room is locked, so that part of the assignment hasn't started.
additional_scenario.complication: The contact says the room is empty, but that doesn't supply access.

conversations.title: The blue bottle isn't identified
conversations.setting: The unreadable-label case at a cleaning cart.
turns: Cleaner
This bottle's label is unreadable, and two products on the cart look similar.
Supervisor
Have you used the bottle, or are you asking before starting that task?
Cleaner
I haven't used it. A colleague recognized the color, but couldn't confirm the contents.
Supervisor
Thanks for stopping to ask. I'll arrange identification or a clearly labeled replacement.
Cleaner
Could you also show me the current product label and Safety Data Sheet for the replacement?
Supervisor
Yes. We'll use information matching the actual product, not a sheet for something similar.
Cleaner
The room task is waiting. Should I describe the delay as a product-information problem?
Supervisor
That's accurate. Don't say the product is defective; we haven't established that.
Cleaner
I'll complete another assigned task that doesn't depend on this bottle while you check.
Supervisor
Good. I'll tell you when the product-information issue is resolved and the task can be reassigned or resumed.

conversations.title: Cleaning isn't a disinfection claim
conversations.setting: A cleaner clarifies a client's description of completed work.
turns: Client
The tables look clean. Can I tell everyone they have definitely been disinfected?
Cleaner
I can confirm the cleaning task I completed, but appearance doesn't establish a disinfection claim.
Client
Our meeting notice uses both words together. I assumed they meant exactly the same thing.
Cleaner
They describe different tasks. My supervisor can confirm the agreed standard for this room.
Client
Please ask them which work was actually included, rather than change the wording by guesswork.
Cleaner
I will. The record shows table cleaning completed; it doesn't document the additional claim you're asking about.
Client
Then I'll say the tables were cleaned while the other question is checked.
Cleaner
That accurately describes what I can confirm from my assignment and completion record.
Client
Could you have the supervisor speak to me if the agreed task needs changing?
Cleaner
Yes. I'll pass on your question about the service standard, not promise a new treatment myself.

conversations.title: A different label on a familiar product
conversations.setting: A cleaner notices a revised product name before starting work.
turns: Cleaner
The replacement container has a different product name from the one on our task sheet.
Team lead
Is it a confirmed replacement on today's list, or just a similar-looking container?
Cleaner
I don't know. The delivery person said it was the new version, but I haven't verified that.
Team lead
Let's check the actual product information and whether the task sheet needs updating.
Cleaner
I'll leave that task pending rather than copy instructions from the previous product.
Team lead
Please identify the old and new names so the supervisor can review the difference.
Cleaner
I've got both names here. The container size is the same, but that doesn't establish equivalence.
Team lead
Correct. We need a confirmed match to the assigned work, not a comparison of bottle size.
Cleaner
I'll ask for the correct label and Safety Data Sheet before using the replacement.
Team lead
I'll arrange that check and let the client know this task hasn't been completed yet.

additional_scenario.title: A borrowed sheet names another product
additional_scenario.brief: A colleague offers a Safety Data Sheet whose product name differs from the container's label. The cleaner has not used the product; the supervisor can locate matching information.
additional_scenario.role_a: Cleaner: point out the exact mismatch.
additional_scenario.role_b: Colleague: accept that a document for a similar product isn't the same record.
additional_scenario.opening_line: The product name on this sheet doesn't match the bottle.
additional_scenario.complication: The colleague says both products perform the same kind of cleaning.

conversations.title: Water beside the east stair door
conversations.setting: The washroom B report in the case.
turns: Cleaner
There's water outside washroom B, beside the east stair door on the ground floor.
Supervisor
Do you know the source, or have you only observed water in that location?
Cleaner
Only the water. I haven't identified a leak or marked the affected area ready.
Supervisor
I'll arrange the site's response. Have you reported the access concern through our usual contact?
Cleaner
Yes, the area concern has been reported, but I need to know who takes the follow-up.
Supervisor
I'll take that contact and tell the response team the exact washroom and stair-door location.
Cleaner
A passerby said the floor was cleaned earlier. That doesn't explain the water now.
Supervisor
Agreed. We'll use the current observation, not assume the earlier cleaning settled today's condition.
Cleaner
What should the hazard report say for the incoming team?
Supervisor
Tell them water was reported, the source is unknown, and I'm coordinating the response.

conversations.title: The noise is not a diagnosis
conversations.setting: A cleaner reports a vacuum problem without repair instructions.
turns: Cleaner
The vacuum labeled C4 made an unfamiliar rattling sound while I was working near reception.
Team lead
Have you stopped using it, and do you know whether anything specific caused the sound?
Cleaner
I've stopped using it. I don't know the cause and haven't attempted a repair.
Team lead
I'll arrange a check and an out-of-service notice for C4, not C14.
Cleaner
The reception carpet task is incomplete. Could you confirm whether another suitable unit is available?
Team lead
I'll check that. Don't report the task complete simply because most of the area was covered.
Cleaner
Understood. The strip beside the visitor chairs remains unfinished, while the open aisle is complete.
Team lead
That distinction helps. I'll assign the remaining strip once an equipment option is confirmed.
Cleaner
Should I tell reception we need a motor replacement, as someone suggested?
Team lead
No. Report the equipment check and incomplete strip; a motor diagnosis hasn't been established.

conversations.title: A recurring mark may need maintenance
conversations.setting: A cleaner reports a recurring ceiling stain without identifying its cause.
turns: Cleaner
The mark above office 5's doorway is visible again after the earlier visit.
Building contact
Are you saying there's a confirmed leak, or just that the mark has returned?
Cleaner
Just that it has returned. I haven't established the source or a repair requirement.
Building contact
I'll pass that observation to maintenance. When did you notice the change today?
Cleaner
At about seven this morning, while completing the corridor assignment outside office five.
Building contact
Is the office itself affected, or did you only observe the corridor-facing area?
Cleaner
I observed the area above the doorway from the corridor. I haven't inspected inside.
Building contact
Then I'll keep the request limited to that location and ask maintenance to assess it.
Cleaner
Please tell me who receives the maintenance request so I can hand over the status accurately.
Building contact
I've accepted it for the building team. Tell the next cleaner assessment is pending with me.

additional_scenario.title: A notice belongs to another machine
additional_scenario.brief: Two floor machines stand together. One has an out-of-service notice identifying unit F3. The second is F8. The cleaner hasn't checked F8's readiness.
additional_scenario.role_a: Cleaner: report F3's notice without assuming F8 is ready.
additional_scenario.role_b: Lead: confirm the exact equipment identifiers and arrange the separate readiness check.
additional_scenario.opening_line: The notice names F3; I haven't confirmed F8's status.
additional_scenario.complication: A colleague treats absence of a notice as proof of readiness.
success_checks: Request confirmation instead of inferring it from appearance.

conversations.title: A case under the chair
conversations.setting: The room 214 lost-property handover.
turns: Attendant
I found a closed black glasses case beneath the chair in room two-fourteen after checkout.
Lost-property receiver
Have you opened it or identified the owner from anything visible on the outside?
Attendant
I haven't opened it. My item description is based only on the outside.
Lost-property receiver
I'll receive it through our lost-property arrangement. Please confirm the found location again.
Attendant
Beneath the chair in two-fourteen, not on the desk or in the corridor.
Lost-property receiver
I've received the closed black case; the custody record will show that found location.
Attendant
A colleague assumed it belonged to the last guest, but that hasn't been confirmed.
Lost-property receiver
We'll keep ownership unconfirmed. Any claimant can speak with the designated team about identification.
Attendant
Do you need anything else from me to complete this transfer record?
Lost-property receiver
Only your confirmation of the observation; I've accepted the item and the follow-up from here.

conversations.title: Papers beside a bin aren't necessarily waste
conversations.setting: A commercial cleaner asks about loose documents.
turns: Cleaner
There are loose papers beside the recycling bin, but they aren't inside it.
Office contact
Have they been marked for disposal, or are you asking because their status is unclear?
Cleaner
Their status is unclear. I haven't read the contents or treated them as waste.
Office contact
Thank you. Those belong to the meeting organizer, who left them for collection.
Cleaner
I'll leave them in place and clean the accessible area around them.
Office contact
Please do. The organizer will move them before your next scheduled visit.
Cleaner
Should I record that this small floor area couldn't be completed because documents blocked access?
Office contact
Yes, describe the blocked area without including any information from the papers themselves.
Cleaner
I'll say the floor beside the recycling bin remains inaccessible due to stored documents.
Office contact
That is enough. I'll arrange their removal without asking you to decide what can be discarded.

conversations.title: A visitor asks for someone else's property
conversations.setting: A cleaner redirects an ownership claim to the designated team.
turns: Visitor
I heard you found a phone in the lounge. Can you give it to me?
Cleaner
The lost-property team handles return requests. I can direct you to their desk.
Visitor
It's probably my colleague's phone. They asked me to collect anything you found.
Cleaner
I can't confirm ownership or release an item from that statement alone.
Visitor
Could you at least tell me whose name appears on the screen?
Cleaner
I haven't inspected private information. Please explain your request to the lost-property team.
Visitor
Where is the desk, and will they know about the item from the lounge?
Cleaner
The reception desk handles these inquiries and can check the relevant record.
Visitor
I'll go there and provide the details they request to assess the claim.
Cleaner
Thank you. They can discuss the return arrangement; I don't need your colleague's personal details here.

additional_scenario.title: Found location versus storage location
additional_scenario.brief: A cleaner found a scarf on the third-floor lounge sofa. It is now held by the designated office on the ground floor. A colleague asks where it was found.
additional_scenario.role_a: Cleaner: distinguish discovery and current custody.
additional_scenario.opening_line: It was found upstairs, but the ground-floor office now holds it.
additional_scenario.complication: The colleague starts recording the ground-floor office as the found location.
success_checks: Name the lounge sofa as the found location.
Name the office as current custody.
Correct the record without adding ownership assumptions.

conversations.title: Only the bath towels are short
conversations.setting: The third-floor cart count from the case.
turns: Attendant
I've counted nine bath towels and eight hand towels on the third-floor cart.
Linen colleague
Our par stock is twelve bath towels and eight hand towels. What's the shortfall?
Attendant
Three bath towels. The hand-towel count is complete, and I haven't reported a general linen stockout.
Linen colleague
A laundry delivery is expected this afternoon, but I don't have a confirmed arrival time.
Attendant
Could you check whether three bath towels can be allocated from stock already available?
Linen colleague
I'll check that now. Are the nine on your cart all assigned to this floor?
Attendant
Yes, none are reserved for another floor or already promised for a separate request.
Linen colleague
Then I'll look for the three-item shortfall rather than send you another full cart allocation.
Attendant
Thank you. Please tell me if the request is accepted or still waiting on delivery.
Linen colleague
I found three available bath towels and can allocate them now; laundry timing remains separate.

conversations.title: A carton count hides the refill type
conversations.setting: A cleaner checks supplies delivered to an office washroom.
turns: Cleaner
Two cartons arrived, but only one has the paper-towel refill type listed for our washroom.
Stores colleague
What's in the other carton? Does its label identify a different dispenser refill?
Cleaner
Yes, it is labeled for the larger dispenser used on the ground floor.
Stores colleague
Then two cartons delivered doesn't mean two suitable cartons for your assigned washroom.
Cleaner
Exactly. I can report one correct carton and one allocation that needs checking.
Stores colleague
I'll review the delivery destination rather than ask you to make the wrong refill fit.
Cleaner
The upper-floor dispensers still need the listed type. Can you check available stock?
Stores colleague
Yes. I'll confirm the correct product code and the number available before promising replenishment.
Cleaner
I'll keep the upper-floor shortage separate from the total number of cartons received.
Stores colleague
That will make the request clear and prevent another delivery of the wrong refill type.

conversations.title: An allocation isn't extra stock
conversations.setting: A room attendant checks whether linen in another cart is available.
turns: Attendant
The neighboring cart has six spare-looking sheets. Can I take two for my assignment?
Team lead
They may already be allocated. Which room tasks are you short on right now?
Attendant
I'm short two sheets against my current assignment, and my own cart has none remaining.
Team lead
Thanks. I'll check that cart's allocation before assuming its visible supplies are spare.
Attendant
I don't want to leave the next attendant short just because their cart looks full.
Team lead
Exactly. The count is six, but the room list shows all six assigned to their floor.
Attendant
Then I need another source for my two, rather than reclassify those sheets as unassigned.
Team lead
I'll check the linen room for available stock and tell you the confirmed amount.
Attendant
Please also confirm whether that changes my room sequence while we wait for supplies.
Team lead
Yes. You can take the supply-independent tasks first; we'll keep the two-sheet shortfall visible.

additional_scenario.title: A changed room allocation changes the target
additional_scenario.brief: An attendant's cart has ten bath towels for a ten-towel assignment. The supervisor adds two rooms requiring four more bath towels under the fictional plan. No extra towels have arrived.
additional_scenario.role_a: Attendant: state the revised target and shortfall.
additional_scenario.role_b: Supervisor: confirm fourteen total and arrange four additional towels.
additional_scenario.opening_line: Does the added assignment raise my bath-towel target from ten to fourteen?
additional_scenario.complication: A colleague counts the original ten as though the new rooms were already covered.
success_checks: Confirm fourteen as the new target.
Keep assignment change separate from delivered stock.

conversations.title: The panel beside office eight
conversations.setting: The glass-quality concern in the case.
turns: Client
There are streaks on the glass you cleaned earlier beside office eight.
Cleaner
Thank you for pointing them out. Is it this interior panel or the outside surface?
Client
This interior panel, especially the upper corner. I'm not referring to the other windows.
Cleaner
I can see the marks you mean. I'll ask our lead to inspect this specific panel.
Client
Can you tell me why they appeared? Was the wrong product used on it?
Cleaner
I don't know the cause. I'll report the visible streaks without guessing about the product.
Client
That's fair. I mainly want the result checked and corrected if it needs rework.
Cleaner
I'll arrange that request through the lead and ask when the panel can be revisited.
Client
Please keep me informed, because the room is free only until the afternoon meeting.
Cleaner
I'll pass on that access limit with the panel location, so the timing can be discussed.

conversations.title: The reported residue is on another desk
conversations.setting: A cleaner checks the precise location of a complaint.
turns: Cleaner
You reported residue on a desk. Could you show me which desk you mean?
Office occupant
The one beside the printer, not the reception desk your colleague looked at.
Cleaner
Thank you. That distinction matters because the two desks have different assignment entries.
Office occupant
I'm not saying the whole office was missed. This is the specific surface I'm concerned about.
Cleaner
I'll report this desk and the visible residue, rather than widen the complaint to the entire office.
Office occupant
Can you deal with it while the papers stay spread across the work surface?
Cleaner
I need the agreed access arrangements. Could the owner clear the affected area first?
Office occupant
I'll ask them now. Please don't move or read the papers to find the mark.
Cleaner
I won't. Once access is available, the lead can confirm the appropriate corrective task.
Office occupant
Good. I'll tell you when the surface is clear so that inspection can take place.

conversations.title: Checking the correction with the occupant
conversations.setting: A cleaner returns after the assigned rework has been completed.
turns: Cleaner
The lead arranged rework on the marked panel. Could you check the area you identified earlier?
Occupant
Yes, this is the corner I meant. The streaks I reported are no longer visible.
Cleaner
Thank you. Does that resolve your original concern about this panel's appearance?
Occupant
It does. I also noticed a separate mark on the door handle, though.
Cleaner
I'll treat that as a new specific concern, not assume the panel correction failed.
Occupant
That's right. The glass issue is resolved; the handle wasn't part of what I showed you.
Cleaner
Could you point to the handle and describe the visible mark for the next request?
Occupant
It's the meeting-room handle, with a small sticky-looking patch near its base.
Cleaner
I'll report that observation to the lead without claiming what the material is.
Occupant
Thank you. Please close the glass concern and keep the handle request separate.

additional_scenario.title: A complaint names the wrong floor
additional_scenario.brief: A client says the second-floor mirror is streaked, then points to a photograph labeled third floor. The cleaner hasn't inspected either mirror.
additional_scenario.role_a: Cleaner: clarify which location the photograph shows.
additional_scenario.role_b: Client: confirm third floor and withdraw the second-floor location.
additional_scenario.opening_line: Before I request rework, which mirror does this photograph identify?
additional_scenario.complication: The client says the mirrors look identical.
success_checks: Avoid reporting both mirrors as defective.
Request inspection of the identified surface.

conversations.title: Three rooms, three statuses
conversations.setting: The end-of-shift case on the third floor.
turns: Outgoing attendant
Room three-oh-one is cleaned. Three-oh-two is cleaned too, but it still awaits the supervisor's inspection.
Incoming attendant
What about three-oh-three? Its room status doesn't show a completed cleaning task.
Outgoing attendant
It was inaccessible, so cleaning hasn't started. Can you take its access follow-up?
Incoming attendant
Yes, I'll check access for three-oh-three and update its status once I know more.
Outgoing attendant
Thank you. I'll confirm the inspection request for three-oh-two with the supervisor before leaving.
Incoming attendant
Then I'm not being asked to release three-oh-two or describe its inspection as complete?
Outgoing attendant
Correct. The supervisor's sign-off is separate. Please focus on checking access to three-oh-three.
Incoming attendant
I'll repeat the status: three-oh-one cleaned; three-oh-two awaiting inspection; three-oh-three uncleaned because access was unavailable.
Outgoing attendant
That's the current picture. Please report any change rather than carry yesterday's assumptions forward.
Incoming attendant
I will. I'll start by contacting the person responsible for access to three-oh-three.

conversations.title: A completed area has one limitation
conversations.setting: A commercial cleaner gives a precise end-of-shift report.
turns: Cleaner
The west office floor is complete except the space beneath the blocked storage shelf.
Incoming colleague
Was that space inaccessible throughout the visit, or did you leave it for another reason?
Cleaner
It was blocked by stored boxes. I wasn't assigned to move them.
Incoming colleague
Then I'll keep that limitation in the completion record rather than mark every area finished.
Cleaner
The office contact has agreed to arrange clearance before tomorrow's visit, but it hasn't happened yet.
Incoming colleague
I'll check whether the boxes are moved before reporting that the remaining area can be reached.
Cleaner
Everything else on that floor's list is complete, including bins and the shared table surfaces.
Incoming colleague
Thanks. Is the blocked area the only outstanding task I'm inheriting for that office?
Cleaner
Yes. The separate maintenance request for the corridor light belongs to the building team.
Incoming colleague
I'll keep the floor limitation and the maintenance request separate in my handover update.

conversations.title: The receiver cannot take the task
conversations.setting: An outgoing cleaner finds that the intended colleague is assigned elsewhere.
turns: Outgoing cleaner
Could you take the final washroom supply check? It hasn't been completed on my shift.
Colleague
I can't accept it yet; I'm assigned to another building for the rest of tonight.
Outgoing cleaner
Thanks for saying so. I won't mark it handed over just because we've discussed it.
Colleague
Please ask the supervisor to reassign it. They know who is staying at this site.
Outgoing cleaner
I'll keep it listed as outstanding and contact them before I finish my report.
Colleague
Tell them the exact washroom and which check is missing so they can allocate it.
Outgoing cleaner
It's washroom C's paper-towel replenishment check, not a new full-room cleaning request.
Colleague
That distinction should help them choose the appropriate worker and avoid duplicating completed cleaning.
Outgoing cleaner
The supervisor has accepted the reassignment question. I'll record that, with the check still unfinished.
Colleague
Good. Someone has the allocation follow-up now, but the supply check itself remains outstanding.

additional_scenario.title: A room number is read incorrectly
additional_scenario.brief: The outgoing attendant says room 416 awaits inspection. The incoming worker repeats 460. Room 460 is on another floor and isn't in this handover.
additional_scenario.role_a: Outgoing attendant: correct the exact room number.
additional_scenario.role_b: Incoming attendant: read back 416 and its pending inspection.
additional_scenario.complication: A noisy corridor makes the final digits hard to hear.

dialogues.title: An extra room appears during the shift
dialogues.setting: A cleaner and client clarify a request that would change the assigned workload.
dialogue: Client
While you're here, could you also clean the training room upstairs? It should only take a moment.
Cleaner
I can ask about adding it. My current assignment covers this floor, with a fixed access window.
Client
The training room just needs a quick tidy. Does calling it quick make it part of the same visit?
Cleaner
Could you describe what needs cleaning? I'll ask my supervisor whether it fits our service scope.
Client
Tables, bins, and the carpet, please. There are about twenty chairs, but they don't need rearranging.
Cleaner
Thank you. Is anyone still using the room, and when would you need the work completed?
Client
A session ends at four. We'd like it ready for tomorrow morning, rather than immediately this afternoon.
Cleaner
That timing helps. I'll ask whether the evening team can take it without interrupting this floor's work.
Client
Please do. I don't want you to leave today's listed rooms unfinished because I mentioned another room.
Cleaner
I'll finish the agreed assignment and pass on the upstairs scope, occupancy, and requested completion time.
Client
Who should confirm the extra visit with me? I need to know whether the request was accepted.
Cleaner
My supervisor will confirm it; I've recorded the request, not booked another visit.
notes: 'Calling it quick' challenges a label without accepting an unsupported estimate.
'Recorded' and 'booked' describe different stages: a request isn't a confirmed additional service.

dialogues.title: A declined visit is not a complaint
dialogues.setting: An attendant checks how to report a guest's decision without adding an unsupported explanation.
dialogue: Attendant
The guest in 206 declined cleaning today but accepted fresh towels. How should I describe the visit?
Supervisor
For the service refusal, record cleaning declined and two towels delivered. Did they ask for anything else?
Attendant
They asked us not to return later today. They didn't complain about the previous cleaning.
Supervisor
Then don't mark it as a cleanliness complaint or assume they're dissatisfied with the service.
Attendant
I had wondered whether they were upset, but that was only my interpretation of their brief answer.
Supervisor
Keep that interpretation out of the service record. The stated preference is enough for the next attendant.
Attendant
Should I leave the room on tomorrow's usual schedule, or does today's refusal cancel future visits too?
Supervisor
Today's statement concerns today. Follow the normal scheduling arrangement and check any separate request about later service.
Attendant
I'll tell the next attendant: two towels delivered, no return visit requested today.
Supervisor
Yes. That prevents another attendant from offering the same visit again this afternoon without a reason.
Attendant
The towels reached the guest at the door, and I didn't enter the room during that delivery.
Supervisor
Include that if our record asks for delivery location. It describes the visit without inventing a motive.
notes: 'Declined' reports a choice neutrally; 'complained' would add a different action.
'For the rest of today' limits the preference to the period the guest actually specified.

dialogues.title: A shorthand instruction needs a task definition
dialogues.setting: A new cleaner asks the lead what an unfamiliar instruction actually requires.
dialogue: Cleaner
The assignment says 'full treatment' for the meeting-room handles. I don't recognize that term on our task list.
Team lead
That's too vague for a new assignment. Which standard task names do you have in your training materials?
Cleaner
They distinguish cleaning from disinfection, but this note doesn't say which task was requested for the handles.
Team lead
I'll clarify the requested standard with the supervisor rather than assume the writer meant both tasks.
Cleaner
Thank you. The client also asked whether a clean appearance proves the second task was completed.
Team lead
It doesn't. We need the actual assigned work and its completion record, not a conclusion from appearance.
Cleaner
Should I tell the client nothing has been done, or explain which part is already complete?
Team lead
Tell them the handles were cleaned under the listed task, while the additional request is still being clarified.
Cleaner
I'll use those words. I don't want the vague phrase to make completed cleaning sound like unfinished work.
Team lead
Exactly. Nor should it turn completed cleaning into a claim about a different task that wasn't confirmed.
Cleaner
Once the supervisor clarifies the extra request, can you tell me who will perform it if it's assigned?
Team lead
Yes. I'll confirm the task and who will do it.
notes: 'Nor should it' introduces a second incorrect inference to avoid.
'Named task' replaces an ambiguous label with a specific assignment; it isn't a chemical instruction.

dialogues.title: An access concern affects only part of a floor
dialogues.setting: A cleaner helps an office contact understand a limited area restriction.
dialogue: Office contact
Someone said the whole second floor is closed because you found a problem. Is that what you reported?
Cleaner
No. I reported water near the east washroom entrance; I didn't report the entire floor as unavailable.
Office contact
Can staff still use every other route, or are you able to confirm that for us?
Cleaner
The site response team needs to confirm access. I can give the precise location, not certify every route.
Office contact
Thank you. The message we heard made it sound as though all cleaning had stopped upstairs.
Cleaner
The west offices are complete. The east washroom entrance remains an unresolved area on my assignment.
Office contact
Who is handling that unresolved area? I need a contact for questions about access during our meeting.
Cleaner
The supervisor has accepted the response follow-up and can connect you with the responsible site team.
Office contact
I'll direct staff questions there, rather than ask you to decide whether a route is suitable.
Cleaner
That helps. I'll also correct the broad report by naming the actual affected entrance and completed west offices.
Office contact
Please mention that the source of the water hasn't been established, so people don't spread a repair diagnosis.
Cleaner
I'll report the observed water, its location, and who is coordinating the response.
notes: 'I didn't report' corrects the scope of a secondhand message without certifying unrelated areas.
'Unresolved area' signals a pending status, not a diagnosis of the building fault.

dialogues.title: The person taking over needs to accept custody
dialogues.setting: An attendant transfers a found bag when the usual receiver is temporarily absent.
dialogue: Attendant
I found an unattended bag in the meeting room, and the usual lost-property receiver isn't at the desk.
Supervisor
Keep the site's arrangements in place. What have you observed, without opening or investigating the bag yourself?
Attendant
It's a small gray fabric bag beside the back row of chairs. I haven't inspected its contents.
Supervisor
Thank you. Don't assume it's abandoned or ordinary waste. I'll arrange the appropriate response for the situation.
Attendant
A conference worker offered to take it, but I don't know whether they are the designated receiver.
Supervisor
Then don't treat that offer as a completed transfer. I'll identify who can accept the follow-up here.
Attendant
Could you also tell them the exact location, so it isn't confused with another report from the lobby?
Supervisor
Yes: meeting room, back row of chairs, gray fabric bag. The lobby report remains separate.
Attendant
I'll keep the found location and my observations clear. I haven't named an owner or searched for identification.
Supervisor
That's appropriate. I've contacted the designated site responder, who has accepted the follow-up and will attend.
Attendant
What should I tell the conference worker while we're waiting for that response to arrive?
Supervisor
Tell them the site responder is handling it, including any ownership claim.
notes: 'An offer' and 'a completed transfer' are different: responsibility needs explicit acceptance.
'Without opening or investigating' limits the report to observations and preserves the site's response boundary.

dialogues.title: Reconciling a linen return
dialogues.setting: Two staff members compare a return count with a cart record.
dialogue: Attendant
The cart record says seven unused hand towels returned, but I counted only six at the receiving point.
Linen colleague
Did you count them here, or are you repeating the number the outgoing attendant mentioned?
Attendant
I counted six here. I haven't established why the record lists seven instead.
Linen colleague
Then let's keep the observed count and recorded count separate while we ask about the difference.
Attendant
A colleague thought one might be on the other cart, but that hasn't been checked yet.
Linen colleague
I'll check with that colleague. We shouldn't change the received count to seven just because the explanation sounds possible.
Attendant
Should I report the discrepancy as a missing towel, or would that imply we've finished looking?
Linen colleague
Report a one-towel discrepancy with the location of the remaining item unconfirmed. The count still needs reconciliation.
Attendant
I can do that. The bath towels match their record, so the question affects hand towels only.
Linen colleague
Good. I'll keep the product types separate and contact the outgoing attendant about the seventh hand towel.
Attendant
They've just confirmed one remained on their cart. Please verify it before adding it to this received count.
Linen colleague
I will. Until it reaches this receiving point and is counted, six remains the quantity actually received here.
notes: 'Received count' differs from the number still held elsewhere.
'A discrepancy' names a mismatch without asserting theft, loss, or a completed investigation.

dialogues.title: A complaint includes a fact and an assumption
dialogues.setting: A cleaner separates a visible concern from a claim about what the earlier team did.
dialogue: Client
The table has a sticky patch, so your evening team must have skipped this whole room.
Cleaner
I can see the patch you're pointing out, but I can't confirm that explanation from the surface alone.
Client
I arrived after another group used the room. I don't know what happened before their meeting.
Cleaner
Thank you, that timing helps. We can report the current patch without deciding who caused it.
Client
I still need it addressed before our next session. Can you arrange a check of this table?
Cleaner
Yes. I'll tell the lead the exact table, the visible condition, and your next-session time.
Client
The next session starts at two. Please don't promise a whole-room clean if only this table needs attention.
Cleaner
Understood. The request concerns this table patch, with any additional work dependent on the lead's assessment.
Client
Will someone confirm the result with me after the assigned correction rather than just tick a box?
Cleaner
I'll ask for a check-back on this specific concern. Who will be available here to review it?
Client
I'll remain at the reception desk until one thirty, and my colleague Dana can review it afterward.
Cleaner
I'll pass on both contacts so someone can check the correction with you.
notes: 'Must have' expresses a strong inference; the cleaner doesn't adopt it without evidence.
'Current patch' focuses the report on the observable issue rather than assigning blame.

dialogues.title: An inspection request is not a release decision
dialogues.setting: An attendant clarifies a room-status question from a reception colleague.
dialogue: Reception colleague
Room 512 shows cleaned. Can I send the waiting guest up?
Attendant
I can confirm cleaning is complete, but the supervisor's inspection hasn't been recorded as finished.
Reception colleague
I saw the inspection request sent ten minutes ago. Doesn't that mean the supervisor accepted and completed it?
Attendant
Not necessarily. I'll check whether the supervisor has accepted the inspection request.
Reception colleague
Please do. I need a reliable status rather than a guess based on how long the request has existed.
Attendant
The supervisor has accepted the inspection and is heading there now. No completion or release is confirmed yet.
Reception colleague
Thank you. I'll tell the guest we're still awaiting the final room-status update, without promising an exact minute.
Attendant
